pr_title: arch: common: multilevel_irq: register directly from driver
pr_body:
#63172 reworked the LUT struct in the `multilevel_irq.c` (formerly `sw_isr_table.c`) to have an additional `struct device` pointer member so that Zephyr can know the controller responsible for an interrupt request by referring to the table.

![Screenshot 2024-04-18 at 10 27 57 AM](https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/assets/1563974/357442dd-de97-4bb3-a438-488e7375ad6b)

The tables generation implementation in #63172 continues to be done directly in the `multilevel_irq.c`, however, it has no knowledge of the interrupt controllers and have to rely on lots of macro magic🧙‍♂️✨ to:

1. Loop through the devicetree, and search for interrupt controllers by looking for the `interrupt-controller` property
2. Find the interrupt controller which IRQ is equals to aggregator interrupt offset defined by the Kconfigs (i.e. `CONFIG_2ND_LVL_INTR_00_OFFSET`)

which is both flimsy and hard to understand.

This PR seeks to flip things around, that is, allow the interrupt controller(s) to register itself with the multilevel LUT by using the `IRQ_PARENT_ENTRY_DEFINE` macro. Additionally, `INTC_ISR_TBL_OFFSET` is made to get the SW ISR table level offset based on the order of the controller.

The LUT, now includes an additional `level` member, is placed directly into the iterable struct section, eliminating the need to have 2 separate tables and additional macro guards in the `multilevel_irq.c`.

This implementation reduces the dependencies on some of the Kconfigs in the `kconfig.multilevel`, the remaining Kconfigs are still required until `gen_isr_table.py` understands the devicetree.

![Screenshot 2024-04-18 at 10 28 11 AM](https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/assets/1563974/9289903e-9b1b-46a9-aa48-4627b10ccc29)

[Migration doc preview](https://builds.zephyrproject.io/zephyr/pr/66877/docs/releases/migration-guide-3.7.html)

Fixes #72979

I'm not sure if this needs to go thru an arch meeting - @andyross @peter-mitsis @dcpleung @fkokosinski @carlocaione

Thanks for the review!

> with most continuing to use the old stuff

Would it help if all multilevel interrupt drivers are updated to use the new implementation?

@andyross - I would not be so pessimistic. My implementation (#66392) is meant to be compatible with the current implementation at the source code level. When more architectures are going to be supported then the user would not be able to notice which implementation is used at the bottom. It is true - that interrupt system was not touched for eons. And now there is a lot of movement. The implementation of the controller based on #67583 would make the current (with all of the changes in #66392) obsolete, so there is nothing to worry about having 4 different implementations in the future. For the time being, from API perspective, I see only 2.

> Would it help if all multilevel interrupt drivers are updated to use the new implementation?

yes, this is how we should do deprecation, calling and existing implementation "legacy" and introducing a new one leaving all users with the "legacy" approach and without a plan is something we do not want to go though. A deprecation in the tree usually triggers a CI failure, here you are deprecating via Kconfig which does not.

When we deprecate something, we want to move all users to the new feature and leave the deprecation warnings ONLY to OOT tree users.
Pulling this back to draft - working on updating existing multilevel interrupt drivers
I've updated all the in-tree interrupt controller drivers that are multi-level(let me know if I missed any), and added a build-only test for all of them

> Just wondering how much have this been tested on actual hardware?

It's been a while, to be on the safe side I'd say this is not tested on a real hardware with full blown application. I also didn't test anything else other than the RISCV PLIC driver.

Unfortunately testing stuff inside meta hasn't been easy and straightforward, I usually rely on upstream Zephyr tools for this.

The following diff will enable both of the UARTs, one on each PLIC in the `riscv32_virtual` renode simulated board, configure the `log_backend_uart` to output on both UART ports, and run a modified `hello_world` sample that uses log:

```diff
(.venv) ycsin@LAPTOP-ROG:~/zephyrproject/zephyr$ git diff --no-prefix 
diff --git boards/renode/riscv32_virtual/riscv32_virtual.dts boards/renode/riscv32_virtual/riscv32_virtual.dts
index 326b9757518..de2814f151a 100644
--- boards/renode/riscv32_virtual/riscv32_virtual.dts
+++ boards/renode/riscv32_virtual/riscv32_virtual.dts
@@ -13,13 +13,23 @@
        compatible = "renode,riscv32-virtual";
 
        chosen {
+               zephyr,log-uart = &log_uarts;
                zephyr,console = &uart0;
                zephyr,shell-uart = &uart0;
                zephyr,flash = &flash0;
                zephyr,sram = &sram0;
        };
+
+       log_uarts: log_uarts {
+               compatible = "zephyr,log-uart";
+               uarts = <&uart0 &uart1>;
+       };
 };
 
 &uart0 {
        status = "okay";
 };
+
+&uart1 {
+       status = "okay";
+};
diff --git boards/renode/riscv32_virtual/support/riscv32_virtual.resc boards/renode/riscv32_virtual/support/riscv32_virtual.resc
index 87e327287b6..60ef8e8b8ef 100644
--- boards/renode/riscv32_virtual/support/riscv32_virtual.resc
+++ boards/renode/riscv32_virtual/support/riscv32_virtual.resc
@@ -8,6 +8,7 @@ mach create $name
 machine LoadPlatformDescription $ORIGIN/riscv32_virtual.repl
 
 showAnalyzer uart0
+showAnalyzer uart1
 cpu PerformanceInMips 4
 
 macro reset
diff --git samples/hello_world/prj.conf samples/hello_world/prj.conf
index b2a4ba59104..3c81a95875c 100644
--- samples/hello_world/prj.conf
+++ samples/hello_world/prj.conf
@@ -1 +1,2 @@
 # nothing here
+CONFIG_LOG=y
diff --git samples/hello_world/src/main.c samples/hello_world/src/main.c
index c550ab461cb..c33dd961cbf 100644
--- samples/hello_world/src/main.c
+++ samples/hello_world/src/main.c
@@ -5,10 +5,17 @@
  */
 
 #include <stdio.h>
+#include <zephyr/logging/log.h>
+#include <zephyr/kernel.h>
+
+LOG_MODULE_REGISTER(main);
 
 int main(void)
 {
-       printf("Hello World! %s\n", CONFIG_BOARD_TARGET);
+       do {
+               LOG_INF("Hello World! %s", CONFIG_BOARD_TARGET);
+               k_msleep(1000);
+       } while (true);
 
        return 0;
 }
```

issue_context.title: `nrf54h20dk/nrf54h20/cpuppr` fails `tests/kernel/gen_isr_table/arch.interrupt.gen_isr_table.riscv_no_direct`
issue_context.body:
**Describe the bug**
`nrf54h20dk/nrf54h20/cpuppr` fails to build the `tests/kernel/gen_isr_table/arch.interrupt.gen_isr_table.riscv_no_direct` test and is currently failing in the CI of #66877

**To Reproduce**
Steps to reproduce the behavior:
1. Check out `main`
2. `west build -b nrf54h20dk/nrf54h20/cpuppr -p auto zephyr/tests/kernel/gen_isr_table -T arch.interrupt.gen_isr_table.riscv_no_direct`
3. See failure

**Expected behavior**
Build should pass in `main` branch

**Impact**
Blocking #66877

**Logs and console output**

```
/Users/ycsin/zephyr-sdk-0.16.5-1/riscv64-zephyr-elf/bin/../lib/gcc/riscv64-zephyr-elf/12.2.0/../../../../riscv64-zephyr-elf/bin/ld.bfd: zephyr/libzephyr.a(vector.S.obj): in function `.L0 ':
```

See the [CI output](https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/actions/runs/9121865587/job/25081815350?pr=66877) of #66877
